Yakuza Remnants.text: Japan's yakuza did not survive the age of heroes intact. In the chaos when Quirks spread, the old crime families grew rich, but as licensed heroes rose and worked with the police, the families were broken one after another: bosses jailed, money seized, territories absorbed into agency patrol routes. The survivors were declared designated villain groups. Their membership is registered with the police, their offices and compounds are watched, and any crime by one member brings scrutiny on the whole group. Most members drifted into ordinary jobs or ordinary crime; a few houses held together around an old boss, a name and a code of loyalty. The remnants live small: gambling dens, loans at hard interest, protection money from shops that remember them, smuggling and the odd job through a broker, all kept quiet enough to stay below a hero's notice. They keep their ceremony: oaths sworn over sake cups, formal ranks, deference to the boss and a habit of settling disputes inside the house. The public sees them as relics, old men in old suits from a vanished era, and most heroes treat them as a police matter. The best known surviving house is the Shie Hassaikai, which keeps a walled compound on the southeastern edge of Osaka. A designated group that draws heroes to its door rarely survives the attention, so every house weighs its ambitions against that risk.
